MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Employment Type: Various Permanent and Temporary Opportunities Available
Position Classification: Registered Nurse
Remuneration: 81748.17 - 114771.98 full-time equivalent base salary range (+12% super + 17.5% leave loading and salary packaging) 
Hours Per Week: up to 38
Requisition ID: REQ679832
Located in: Randwick
Applications Close: Opportunity will remain open for applications until vacancies are filled. Interviews and appointments will be taking place during this period. 
For role related queries or questions contact Michelle Hughes on Michelle.Hughes@health.nsw.gov.au

 

At the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network, every role helps children and young people live their healthiest lives.

As the largest paediatric health service in Australia, we care for thousands of children each year, in hospital and at home. Our people are united by compassion, collaboration and excellence in care.

Sydney Children's Hospital (SCH), Randwick, one of Australia's leading specialist centres for children, has entered an exciting new chapter with the opening of the Bilima Building in November 2025.

This state-of-the-art redevelopment enhances our ability to deliver world-class care to seriously ill and injured children from across NSW and beyond. 

We are seeking nurses to join our 18-bed tertiary Paediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU), caring for critically ill infants, children and young people requiring highly specialised and complex care, supported by a skilled multidisciplinary team. We are committed to supporting your success in this challenging and rewarding specialty. You will be welcomed into a strong, approachable leadership team and benefit from structured education, dedicated preceptorship and supported clinical development. For nurses new to the PICU environment, we offer a tailored Specialist Transition Program (STP), designed to build your confidence, knowledge and clinical capability in intensive care nursing. 

As part of the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network, SCH provides a comprehensive range of paediatric and adolescent medical and surgical services, caring for children with a wide variety of complex conditions. Located in Sydney's eastern suburbs and co-located with Prince of Wales Hospital and the Royal Hospital for Women, our campus offers easy access to beaches, amenities and public transport. 

You'll be part of a warm, supportive culture focused on excellence in care and improving outcomes for children and their families.

To be eligible to apply for this position, applicants must hold a valid visa with unrestricted working rights in Australia, or be an Australian citizen or permanent resident.

What you'll be doing
 

The Registered Nurse provides safe, compassionate, person-centred care to patients and families of Sydney Children's Hospital Network. 
The Registered Nurse acts as a role model by demonstrating behaviour and interacting with patients, their families and employees in a way that promotes a culture and standards that reflect the NSW Health CORE values of Collaboration, Openness , Respect and Empowerment. 

 

Additional Benefits (where applicable): Flexible work opportunities, Salary packaging and meal entertainment benefits, accrued days off (ADOs), fitness passport, employee assistance program (EAP)

How to Apply:
Click 'Apply Online' and submit your application including:

A resume (maximum 5 pages) outlining your experience 

Responses to the questions below:

Current Authority to Practice as a Registered Nurse with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA).

Recent critical care experience and-or recent paediatric experience.

Demonstrated excellent verbal, written and interpersonal skills.

Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary team.

Effective time management skills

Computer literacy.

Capacity to work a seven (7) day rotating roster including public holidays and reasonable overtime.

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

Child Safe Standards:
SCHN is committed to maintaining a child-safe environment that respects and upholds the rights of children and young people, in line with NSW Health's commitment to the Child Safe Standards. We aim to ensure that children and young people feel safe, supported, and included in their care. All current and prospective staff are expected to prioritise the safety, welfare, and well-being of children and young people, actively working to protect them from harm and abuse.

Additional Information: 

SCHN is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values diversity, recognising that a diverse workforce strengthens our culture and enhances the care we provide to children, young people and their families.

Permanent NSW Health roles require Australian citizenship or permanent residency. Temporary visa holders may be considered where no suitable Australian citizen or permanent resident is identified.

NSW Health vaccination and screening requirements must be met prior to commencement. 

This position requires a Working with Children Check (WWCC) issued by the Office of the Children's Guardian.

Where required, overseas qualifications must be formally assessed by the Department of Education or relevant authority for recognition in Australia.

An Eligibility List may be created for future permanent and temporary full or part time vacancies. 

Need more information? 
 1) Click here for the Position Description
 2) Find out more about applying for this position

 

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people are strongly encouraged to apply. We recognise the value of Aboriginal staff providing health care to Aboriginal children and families. For application support, visit the NSW Health Aboriginal Recruitment tool, Stepping Up to assist in preparing your application, or contact the SCHN's Aboriginal Workforce Consultant at SCHN-EA-AboriginalHealthDirectorate@health.nsw.gov.au

For technical support please contact 1300 679 367

Keep Learning on Track - Support the Systems that Support Our Workforce

Looking for a role where organisation, technology and customer support come together? Join our team as a Training Support Officer and play a key role in supporting learning and workforce capability across regional South Australia.

About the Role

In this role, you'll provide frontline support to end users, managers and facilitators while helping ensure training systems and records remain accurate, accessible and efficient. From creating user accounts and managing training access to processing recognition of prior learning (RPL) requests and maintaining attendance and completion records, your work will directly support the delivery of workforce learning outcomes.

About You

You are a proactive and customer-focused professional who thrives in a fast-paced environment and enjoys solving problems. You bring:

Strong interpersonal, written and verbal communication skills with the ability to provide high-quality customer support.

Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.

Demonstrated experience working independently and collaboratively within a team environment.

High-level computer literacy, including troubleshooting and proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.

Experience preparing reports, maintaining systems and procedures, and managing sensitive or confidential information.

Experience working with Learning Management Systems (LMS) such as Moodle, WorldLearn or similar platforms will be highly regarded.

About Us

Yorke and Northern Local Health Network (YNLHN) is committed to an inclusive and diverse workplace and encourages applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, culturally diverse backgrounds, LGBTIQA+SB communities, and people living with disability and-or neurodivergence. We support workplace adjustments and welcome you to share any access or support needs during recruitment and employment. Flexible working arrangements, including part-time options, may be available and can be discussed for this role.

A career in YNLHN offers diverse opportunities, strong career development, and the chance to live and work across a unique landscape including farming regions, coastline, vineyards, and the Southern Flinders Ranges. View the video below to learn more about working with us

Work with us - Yorke and Northern LHN

result.description:
Community Worker

Business: CoreAssist Pty Ltd
Location: Yagoona NSW 2199
Employment Type: Full-time, Ongoing
Salary: AUD $75,000 – $85,000 per annum plus superannuation

Full Job Description

About the Business
CoreAssist Pty Ltd is a registered NDIS provider based in Yagoona, New South Wales, delivering personalised disability support services to participants across Sydney, Western Sydney, and surrounding communities. The organisation provides a broad range of services including Supported Independent Living (SIL), daily living assistance, support coordination, community participation, life skills development, mental health support, aged care, transport assistance, household tasks, home modifications, and specialised disability support programs. 
CoreAssist is committed to empowering people living with disabilities to achieve greater independence, social inclusion, and improved quality of life through person-centred, culturally responsive, and outcome-focused support services. The organisation works collaboratively with participants, families, carers, allied health professionals, support coordinators, and community organisations to deliver tailored support solutions aligned with individual goals and NDIS plans. CoreAssist operates under strong values of compassion, integrity, inclusiveness, accountability, innovation, and respect while maintaining full compliance with NDIS Practice Standards and relevant Australian legislation. 
As demand for disability and community support services continues to increase, CoreAssist requires an experienced Community Worker to coordinate participant supports, facilitate community engagement, promote independence, and ensure participants receive high-quality, person-centred services that enable them to achieve their personal goals.

About the Role
The Community Worker is responsible for assessing participant needs, developing and implementing individual support strategies, coordinating access to community resources, monitoring participant progress, and assisting individuals living with disabilities to maximise independence and community participation.
Working closely with participants, families, allied health professionals, support coordinators, healthcare providers, and external agencies, the Community Worker plays an important role in delivering holistic support that promotes inclusion, wellbeing, personal development, and positive participant outcomes consistent with CoreAssist's person-centred service model. 
The position requires excellent communication, interpersonal, organisational, and problem-solving skills together with a genuine commitment to improving the lives of people living with disabilities.

Key Responsibilities
•	Conduct participant interviews and comprehensive needs assessments to identify individual goals, strengths, risks, and support requirements.
•	Develop, implement, monitor, and regularly review individual support plans consistent with participant goals and NDIS plans.
•	Support participants to develop independent living skills, social skills, confidence, and community participation.
•	Assist participants to access healthcare, allied health, housing, education, employment, transport, recreational, and other community support services.
•	Facilitate participant involvement in community activities, life skills programs, recreational programs, and social inclusion initiatives.
•	Monitor participant wellbeing, evaluate service outcomes, maintain accurate case notes, and prepare progress reports.
•	Provide advocacy, information, guidance, and practical assistance to participants and their families regarding available community services and supports.
•	Liaise with support coordinators, allied health professionals, healthcare providers, government agencies, carers, and community organisations to coordinate integrated service delivery.
•	Identify barriers affecting participant independence and implement appropriate support strategies to promote positive outcomes.
•	Maintain confidential participant records, service documentation, incident reports, and case management records in accordance with NDIS Practice Standards and organisational policies.
•	Promote participant rights, dignity, choice, privacy, cultural inclusion, and person-centred practice at all times.
•	Participate in multidisciplinary meetings, quality improvement initiatives, and ongoing professional development.
•	Assist CoreAssist in maintaining compliance with NDIS Practice Standards, Work Health and Safety legislation, Child Safe requirements, and organisational policies.
•	Support continuous improvement initiatives that enhance participant satisfaction, service quality, and organisational performance.


Requirements
•	Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
•	AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma in Community Services, Disability, Human Services, Welfare, Individual Support, or a closely related field, or at least three years of relevant experience may substitute for formal qualifications where applicable (ANZSCO Skill Level 2).
•	Demonstrated experience working within disability services, community services, aged care, or NDIS-funded programs.
•	Strong understanding of person-centred practice, participant rights, safeguarding principles, and community service delivery.
•	Sound knowledge of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS), disability support services, community resources, and participant-centred care.
•	Excellent communication, interpersonal, and relationship-building skills.
•	Strong organisational, problem-solving, and case coordination abilities.
•	Ability to maintain accurate participant records and prepare professional reports.
•	Compassionate, empathetic, reliable, and participant-focused approach to service delivery.
•	Ability to work independently and collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams.
•	Current NDIS Worker Screening Check, National Police Check, Working with Children Check (where applicable), and Current First Aid/CPR certification or willingness to obtain.
•	Current Australian Driver Licence is desirable.

Work Conditions
•	Full-time, ongoing position.
•	Standard operational hours with flexibility based on participant needs and service delivery requirements.
•	Work is performed across participant homes, community settings, CoreAssist facilities, and outreach locations throughout Sydney.
•	Ongoing professional development and training opportunities.
•	Collaborative and supportive multidisciplinary environment committed to empowering participants and promoting independence.
•	Opportunity to contribute to meaningful community outcomes through high-quality, person-centred disability support services.

Position: Chef
Type: Full-time
Employer: Java Spice World Pty Ltd
Location: Swan Hill VIC 3585
Salary: $80,000 p/a
About the Business:
Java Spice World Pty Ltd is a premier fully licensed Thai restaurant located in Swan Hill, Victoria, renowned for delivering authentic South East Asian cuisine inspired by the owners’ extensive travels through Thailand, Malaysia, and Indonesia. Established in 2005, the restaurant features unique hand-crafted buildings imported from Java using traditional Teak and Bangkerai hardwoods, combined with tropical gardens and gazebos to create a warm, welcoming ambience that reflects the hospitality encountered across the region. Committed to using the freshest ingredients, no MSG, and accommodating dietary needs (including gluten-free options and spice adjustments), Java Spice values quality, authenticity, and exceptional customer service in a supportive, family-oriented workplace culture that encourages creativity and teamwork.
About the Position:
The Chef plays a pivotal role at Java Spice World Pty Ltd, leading the kitchen team to deliver high-quality, authentic Thai and South East Asian dishes that delight customers through both dine-in and take-away services. This full-time position encompasses creative menu development, precise culinary execution, efficient kitchen operations, and team leadership to maintain the restaurant’s reputation for excellence, consistency, and profitability while upholding strict food safety and hygiene standards.
Key Responsibilities:
Prepping ingredients, cooking menu items, and assembling dishes according to established recipes and plating standards.
Designing seasonal menus, testing new recipes, and updating offerings based on ingredient costs, availability, and customer feedback.
Inspecting all dishes before they leave the kitchen to ensure they meet quality, taste, and presentation standards.
Taking stock of raw materials, tracking shortages, and placing orders with suppliers while managing food and labour costs to minimise waste.
Directing the work of junior chefs, line cooks, and kitchen porters; delegating tasks, training, and mentoring staff on food handling, safety, and techniques.
Enforcing strict health, food safety, sanitation regulations, and allergen control procedures across the kitchen.
Organising duty rosters and ensuring the kitchen is fully staffed during peak hours while maintaining equipment.
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Certificate IV in Hospitality (Commercial Cookery) or equivalent.
Minimum 1 year relevant experience.
Strong technical skills in Thai/South East Asian cuisine preparation, menu development, cost control, and kitchen management.
Excellent leadership and team supervision abilities with a focus on training and mentoring.
Commitment to food safety, hygiene, allergen management, and delivering high-quality customer-focused service.
Ability to work efficiently under pressure in a fast-paced environment.
How to Apply:
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
